items.en: Dull thuds, nearly subsonic, were felt through the armored mass. Breaching charges. When the marines finally broke the vault proper, it was with overwhelming force of sound and light. No unsuited human could withstand the assault on the senses. They were blinded, in shock.

The raid pivoted on mere minutes of chaos. Comms across the hemisphere crackled with static; only tightbeam relays could pierce the rain of EM scatter amid clouds of chaff and disruption. Casualty reports rolled in, displays on the bridge bleeding to fill the volume with a bloody glow.

The marine squads withdrew, leaving broken bulkheads and blaring alarms amid the sporadic return-fire. The MUNISEC were still mobilizing to lock down the port when the last raider shuttle lifted. Its jets kicked up dust that mixed with the leaking atmo.

Kazeron was rich in exotic metals, the former core of a gas giant blasted away in an ancient celestial catastrophe. Its industrial base, built to feed the Domain's Persean frontier heavy machinery and terraforming plant, was quickly adapted to build a warfleet which gave pause to the XIVth Battlegroup.

The small ocean-moon of Fikenhild was the political center of the system, seat of the King and representative to the Persean League. The great floating arcologies glittered night and day, homes to the highly esteemed holo-entertainment studios of Westernesse.

More than a company town, Ilm was a company world, from the orbital security platforms shining above to the teleoperated mines ripped deep down into the crust. Ruled by a semi-militarized corporate board, the identity of investors was not public information, though the least paranoid speculation favored a mix of League and Tri-Tachyon capital.

A vice squad brute stared down all who entered. They could shut the place down at any time, but the teahouse-speakeasy provided a conduit with the commerce required for holy war. Inside was dim and crowded; the stench of drug fumes and cheap liquor competed with a disdain for modern enzyme soap.

They led you through a town of plastered brick and corroded salvage. Bright paint and lush gardens managed, just, to stave off a sense of decay.

Before long you stood before large doors of etched metal. The militants were met by another pair, similarly armed. The most senior lowered his mask.

Chalcedonian architecture trended toward cyclopeanism on the surface. Below, protected from the storms, were the same cheap prefabs seen on poor worlds across the Sector.

The rain sent nasty rivulets of fluid slithering down conduits to pool on moldy canopies. The sky's feeble light diffused into a flattening murk.

There was a cluster of neat, low structures; earthworks and hull panels spotted with forgeglass, sprouting vents. The streets were clean and the citizenry uniformed by job role. Despite fixing outsiders with open stares, they did not falter in their assignments.

It cannot be said to thrive, but the colony of Sentinel gained a new sense of hope and energy after reintegration with the Hegemony.

The citizens were diligent, orderly, and disciplined. It was thought that they would make good officer candidates despite quiet objections from Eventide's old guard.

A Leviathan from out of time, familiar at once from its depictions in the post-Domain Persean Sector. The magisterial force hushes and humbles officers and crew. It makes them reverent, as if they found themselves before the corpse of a thunderous, cruel god who once ruled the skies.

To awaken it, to touch the divine, must fall somewhere between sacrilege and sanctification.

These were the massive, automated starships which bore the Gates that established near-instantaneous connections between distant stars. After a journey of countless lonely cycles, the Gate would be emplaced in a new system and activated, thence to disgorge an explosion of newcomers seeking resources, data, and experiences to feed the grand economy and culture of the Human Domain.
"If it's just followin' orders, it's not me that's going against the convention. Then it's on the captain. Right?"

A spatter of hollowed icons represented dead targets across the display. The last one, full and red, blinked out into a scabrous brown.

A subtle gesture collapsed the image and the icons winked out as one. The holomatrix snowed, then reformed into nav mode, the fleet holding station in low orbit.

When Loke came from the Abyss /
The first world, he burned /
The second, he took without a shot /
The third- look out, there he is!
"The contract can suck vacuum. No credits, no crew."
A navigation buoy dating to the Domain era monitored local system hyperfield topography. The telemetry was of great use to configure and tune fleet drive bubbles.

I asked what drew him back out there, time and time again. The old spacer took a long time before he answered.

"Because it's clean," he said.

The Domain-era array could passively monitor an entire star system and had a transmitter capable of encrypted real-time FTL data transmission to friendly fleets. The telemetry would supplement fleet-based sensors, effectively increasing their power and range.

Makeshift sensor arrays built using post-Collapse technology passively monitored entire star systems. An on-board transmitter was capable of encrypted real-time, FTL data transmission to friendly fleets. This telemetry would supplement fleet-based sensors, effectively increasing their power and range.

The Galatia Academy is the most prestigious university in the Persean Sector. The office of provost directs teaching and research and draws upon alumni to influence new generations of the brightest - or richest - students.
"Don't be too impressed, walker. It's a dim imitation of God's first day."

It appeared empty at first. A colossal tomb, never filled.

Drone-mounted radar drew a ghostly schematic while suit lights piled beams into the echoing volume, catching drifts of dust and gas set aloft by the opening. Cables gleamed in the dark, snaking along the long ranks of coffers.
"It is said that an ex-salvor is either old or rich, never both."

"It's finding the pieces that's the worst. Not so much out there, frozen or fried, but those bits that stick on 'til you're back inside."

"Doesn't smell much at first but after a few shifts you need to run a mil-grade dehaz on all your kit. Can't stand it."

A huge structure loomed, the monolithic facets of its hull scarred by countless cycles of space weathering. The hangars were large enough to hide a vast store of valuable commodities.
Or, perhaps, a fleet of moderate size.

You stood together at last in the plaza under the archway of the Cathedral of Holy Exodus.

"And it is the seat of not more than a few heretical notions of doctrine, I'm afraid," he said in a low voice.

Among towering columns were affixed recovered landing pods of the early Luddic refugee ships, now integrated into the vaults, painted with gilt and green, bedecked with candles and hanging glass ornaments which broke the beams of the sun - filtered through ranks of high windows - into thousands of rainbow shards endlessly refracting.

It was an ecstasy of light, a galaxy unto itself.

A cold light filled the viewscreen, stark against the utter darkness of the hyperspace abyss. It seemed to pulse, shifting dimmer and then brighter, following no discernable pattern. It did not flicker like a flame, nor like a failing comms signal, but like something flitting at the very edge of consciousness...

Cold light began to grow in the primary display. A subtle pulse begged for attention.

A call of alarm, a flare of red, and a pause as the bridge officers took in the eruption of alerts that spilled across their display interfaces.

Haz-suited technicians tended the containment machinery, stepping over coils of tube and wire. A mess of makeshift components were pulled from the common microforge libraries then torn apart and re-engineered to operate in this unusual, even extraordinary, application.

Often filled with recoverable goods, even operational cryopods, a clutch of cargo pods in open space are a tempting target to scavengers. 

Trade convoys fleeing pirates sometimes dump cargo in the hope that their pursuers will power down their engines and content themselves with easy plunder.

These megastructures once powered the unfathomable industrial might of the Domain, putting the human civilization well toward Kardashev type II status. It is capable of extracting energy on an astronomical scale directly from the linked star.

"Those who awake from cryosleep who were laid to rest in the time of the Domain are perhaps the most lost of all. Many, though not all, imagined they would populate the far end of a rich frontier; they accepted that they would leave behind all they once knew. Now they all find themselves cut loose from all reference, unmoored in history."

It was a common class of probe used for research, surveying, and surveillance, the sort of hardware used by civilian enterprise and research institutions. Often run without an active transponder so as not to invite opportunistic scavengers, an active ping will return the ID-packet required both under interfactional commerce law and by most credible insurance combines.

Target profile resembles a phase-enabled hull on a theoretically impossible scale; likely highly unstable. Sensors indicate capital-equivalent weapon loadout in addition to anomalous readings suggesting one or more unknown technology systems. Tactical analysis adjunct cannot determine role of unknown technology. Extreme caution advised.

It doesn't take a detailed survey to ascertain that this is a planet rich in transplutonic ore: the remains of a crude, automated mining-refining operation sprawl like an uncontrolled growth across the surface. It is withered now, the fusion reactors left cold, hundreds of autoforged kiloton teleminer units like dead beetles seemingly swept into drifts by a titanic wind.

This world’s battered crust of cyclopean debris criss-crossed by kilometers-deep pits and chasms is bombarded with intense radiation on the day side, so habitats and industrial facilities must be built deep beneath the surface. The population of Sindria is concentrated in a handful of hive-cities where living conditions for most are poor and civil law harsh. A desperate underclass lives beneath those who are lucky enough to have found positions in the state bureaucracy or miltech incorporates. Infrastructure has never kept up with the population crisis of massive refugee immigration during the Askonia Crisis as resources have been concentrated on industry and military power.

The world's crust is squeezed and cracked by the powerful tidal forces of Salus, causing regular quakes and eruptions. Abundant geysers of volatile gases maintain a thin, toxic atmosphere and combine with iron compounds to give Cruor its sanguine colouration. Tracked rigs roam the more stable surface provinces, ripping out rare or merely convenient ores for export while corroding ruins of machines can occasionally be seen amidst the scars of strip-mining. Dark rumors circulate about the conditions of mobile labor camps operated by Diktat Intelligence.
